solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pole in American airspace

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for the south pole
US, short for United States, stands for American

explanation.surface: A query about a polar station sitting in American airspace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airspace' looks like part of the geography but is the definition: a cavity of air in the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity in the facial bones filled with air is literally a space for air.

clue.text: One picking up litter from field

definitions.text: One picking up litter from field

parts.words: One picking up litter from field
parts.note: litter is an old word for a stretcher, and the field is a battlefield where the wounded are carried off

explanation.surface: Someone tidying rubbish off a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like rubbish but means a stretcher; 'field' is a field of battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who carries the wounded away on a stretcher, especially in war.

clue.text: New Critic losing head gets push

indicators.note: losing head says the word for critic drops its first letter

parts.note: a judge assesses and criticises, so is a critic

explanation.surface: A fresh reviewer, being sacked, is given a shove.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle prod with the elbow is a small push.

clue.text: Wurst from Brownshirts convention?

parts.note: the SA, Sturmabteilung, were the Nazi stormtroopers known as Brownshirts
usage is established custom, convention

explanation.surface: Some German sausage served at a Nazi rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Wurst is the German word for this meat product, keeping the German theme.

clue.text: Oxford grammarian and publisher offering course

parts.note: C. T. Onions was an Oxford grammarian and editor of the Oxford English Dictionary
OUP is Oxford University Press, the publisher

explanation.surface: An Oxford scholar and his publisher putting out something together.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Talbut Onions edited the OED; the Oxford setting points both pieces at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A soup is served as one course of a meal, such as the starter.

clue.text: Exclusively working with vergers in Ledbury

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: read as verge-rs, things on the verges, so the edge letters of the town's name are taken

explanation.surface: Church officers working only in a Herefordshire market town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vergers' looks like church caretakers; it is a whimsical word for the edges. Ledbury is a town in Herefordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Solely, and nothing else: an adverb of restriction.

clue.text: Linda occasionally gets in close to cow

indicators.note: gets in says these letters are placed inside the word for close

parts.note: close friends are intimate

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only some letters of the name, every other one

explanation.surface: Linda now and then cosies up to a cow on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes I and D from Linda; 'gets in' puts them inside INTIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to frighten them into submission, a verb of bullying.

clue.text: Endlessly making claims about woman

indicators.note: about says the shortened word is turned round, read backwards
endlessly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: alleging is making claims

explanation.surface: Someone forever making claims about a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts ALLEGING to ALLEGIN; 'about' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as of the cookery writer Nigella Lawson, and a woman's name stands for a woman.

clue.text: Get bag and boil it to prepare parts required

indicators.note: to prepare a dish the ingredients are worked into new shape, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: boil the food in its bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' are musical parts, not ingredients.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, an obbligato is an instrumental part that must not be left out; this is its plural.

clue.text: Reproduction Stonehenge assembled in capital

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the capital

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France

indicators.note: assembled means put together in a fresh arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A replica of Stonehenge built in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reproduction' reads as a copy of the monument, but it is the biological sense; 'assembled' gives THENOGENES.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin birth: offspring developing from an unfertilised egg is a form of breeding.

clue.text: Swimmer embarrassed by hairstyle

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
a mullet is a hairstyle short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: A swimmer blushing over an unfortunate haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fish of the goatfish family, and fish are swimmers in crossword shorthand.

clue.text: Actress in Georgia with black men

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers, the men

explanation.surface: An actress working in Georgia alongside some black men.
explanation.definitionFit: Zsa Zsa and Eva Gabor were Hungarian-born Hollywood film stars.

clue.text: Old Egyptian at that point holding sailor back

indicators.note: holding says one word keeps another clasped inside it

parts.note: at that point in time means then

indicators.note: back says the word for sailor is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: An ancient Egyptian, back then, restraining a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Thebes was a city in Egypt as well as in Greece, so the clue specifies Egyptian.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Thebes, the ancient capital of Upper Egypt, was an Egyptian of old.

clue.text: Somewhat petty complaint rejected in break

indicators.note: in says the reversed piece sits inside the word for break

parts.note: to smash something is to break it

indicators.note: rejected says the word for complaint is thrown back, read backwards

parts.note: an ill is an ailment or complaint

explanation.surface: A minor grievance turned down during a rest break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns ILL into LLI, placed in SMASH.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix -ish means rather, and small means petty, so it is a mild degree of pettiness.

clue.text: Transport gold to Alabamian settlement

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
Mobile is a port city in Alabama

explanation.surface: Shipping gold off to a town in Alabama.
explanation.definitionFit: A car is a means of transport, a vehicle.

clue.text: Risky vehicle departs after diversion on boundary

indicators.note: on in a down or across clue means placed after, so the boundary word comes first
after puts the abbreviation for departs at the end of the word for diversion

parts.note: a hedge marks the boundary of a field
a diversion is an amusement, fun
D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables

explanation.surface: A dangerous car leaving after a detour around a hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicle' means investment vehicle, not a car.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment vehicle using speculative strategies to chase high returns is notoriously risky.

clue.text: Involving muck but little brass?

parts.note: a play on the Yorkshire saying where there's muck there's brass, brass meaning money

explanation.surface: A dirty job that pays poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' is northern English slang for money; the saying links dirty work with wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely inexpensive, costing very little money.

clue.text: Stove cool for second time

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of heavy cast-iron cooking stove
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A stove cools off a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a range cooker common in British country kitchens.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means once more, on a repeat occasion.

clue.text: Country run by prominent Russian banker?

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the Ural is a major Russian river, and a river is a banker because it has banks

explanation.surface: A nation run by a leading Russian financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is the crossword sense of something with banks: a river, here the Ural.
explanation.definitionFit: Country as an adjective, as in country life, means relating to the countryside.

clue.text: Clear criminal linked to New York theft

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of shape, rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal cleared over a New York robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for stealing property.

clue.text: We go ninth after switch in wide position

indicators.note: after a switch the letters of the phrase are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A batting order change sending someone ninth into a wide field position.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a player out wide near the touchline plays as a winger, out on the flank.

clue.text: Irrational, copper being brought in before hedonist

indicators.note: being brought in says these pieces are placed inside the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
pi is the best-known irrational number
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An unreasonable police officer arrested ahead of a pleasure seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' looks like an adjective but is the noun pi; 'copper' is the metal, not a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to refined pleasures of food and drink is a pleasure seeker.

clue.text: Delay allowed returning books about small snail

indicators.note: about says the reversed word goes round the abbreviation for small
returning says the word for delay allowed is read backwards

parts.note: a period of grace is a delay allowed before payment
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A late return of library books concerning a small snail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns GRACE into ECARG; 'about' puts it round S to give ESCARG.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for an edible snail, served as a delicacy.

clue.text: Writer who's posh leaving Bedfordshire town on M1

indicators.note: on tells the solver the town without posh is joined to the motorway name, which leads

parts.note: M1 is read as the letters M and I, the figure one looking like I

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for posh departs from the town's name

parts.note: Luton is a town in Bedfordshire, an English county north of London
U stands for upper class, posh

explanation.surface: An author with airs who quits a Bedfordshire town on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton really is on the M1, Britain's main motorway north from London; here the M1 is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton was the English poet who wrote Paradise Lost.

clue.text: Member's part in Parliament ultimately wasted?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so the final letter is used

parts.note: wasted is slang for drunk or stoned, high

explanation.surface: Is an MP's role in Parliament a waste in the end?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like an MP; it is a limb, the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is a member of the body, and the upper leg is part of that limb.

clue.text: Map course in vessel circling lake

indicators.note: circling says the vessel goes round the letter for lake

parts.note: a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: Charting a voyage in a boat around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To chart or mark out a route is a verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Magistrate contributing to bizarre evening

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A magistrate playing a part in a strange night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in medieval England with judicial duties, like a sheriff.

clue.text: Series from suicidal novel blocked by Universal

indicators.note: blocked by says the letter for Universal is lodged inside the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal, suitable for all

explanation.surface: A TV series adapted from a novel about suicide, made by Universal studios.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges SUICIDAL to ICLAUDIS; 'blocked by' puts U into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated 1976 BBC television drama series about Rome, from Robert Graves's novel.

clue.text: Salesman still has time to collar people for rebate

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: to collar is to grab round the neck, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: ay is an old word meaning ever, always, still
men are people

explanation.surface: A salesman still finding time to buttonhole people for a refund.
explanation.walkthrough: AY as 'still' is an old poetic sense meaning always, rarely met outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is money handed back, a paying back of an amount.

clue.text: English army getting back to front shows spirit

indicators.note: getting back to front says the last letter of the word for army moves round to the front

parts.note: a host is an army, as in the heavenly host

explanation.surface: An English army retreating to the front line shows spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a group or era.
